transcript.text: Hi there! I'm here with you. I've got the meeting up on my screen and ready to help you catch up on anything you need to know. What would you like to hear about?
Hey, it's Jordan. I had to duck out of the product review meeting - is there any way you could fill me in on what I'm missing?

Hey Jordan! So far they've covered the kickoff slide, and I've got a few key updates for you. Atlas launch is confirmed for September eighteenth—Dana from product confirmed that. And on the backend migration, Marcus from engineering says they're at eighty percent done, with the billing service being the remaining piece, which should take about two weeks. They're still working through the Q three roadmap, launch date, and budget items on the agenda, so let me know if you want me to keep an eye out for anything specific.
Oh great, thanks for catching me up. So September eighteenth for Atlas - that's good to know. What about the onboarding A/B test? Did they mention any results from that yet?
Yes, they did! Priya shared results from the onboarding A/B test—they've improved the drop-off rate from thirty-four percent down to nineteen percent, which is a really solid improvement.
That's awesome, way better than I expected! Nineteen percent is solid. Hey, did anyone talk about the CDN contract renewal? I know that's coming up soon.

Yes, they did cover that—it came up as a key risk. The CDN contract expires August 30th, so it needs to be renewed before the Atlas launch on September 18th. Marcus has taken ownership of that with an August 15th deadline to get it sorted.

Perfect timing—the meeting just wrapped up, so I've got the full recap for you. Atlas launch is locked in for September 18th. Engineering's at eighty percent on the backend migration with just the billing service left—about two weeks of work. Design crushed it with the onboarding flow, dropping the drop-off rate from thirty-four down to nineteen percent. Marketing's also getting an extra one hundred fifty thousand dollars for the launch campaign. On the risk side, the CDN vendor contract expires August 30th and needs renewal before launch—Marcus is owning that with an August 15th deadline. Priya's shipping onboarding v2 by August 1st, and user research sessions got moved to July 28th and 29th. Oh, and one more thing: they approved hiring two more engineers in Q4. They'll share the full notes after the call.

Wait, marketing got an extra hundred fifty thousand? That's exactly what I needed to know. Alright, sounds like you covered everything I was worried about - Atlas timing, the A/B test results, and Marcus handling the CDN renewal. Really appreciate you keeping tabs on all that for me!

Awesome, glad I could help you stay in the loop! You've got everything you need—the meeting's all wrapped up and the notes will come through after we hang up. Anything else you want me to clarify before you head back?
